title: Textures & UV Mapping 🖼️
description: Import images, sample them, control tiling, and understand UV coordinates.

slides.title: What is a Texture? 🏞️
slides.content:
# Pixels on the Surface

A **texture** is a 2D image that materials use to vary colour, roughness, etc. across a surface.

* **Base Color / Albedo** – the main colour image
* **Normal Map** – purple‑ish image that simulates bumps and details
* **Roughness / Metallic / AO** – often packed into a single texture (channels)

Textures are imported into Unreal just like any other asset: drag and drop into the Content Browser. Supported formats: PNG, JPG, TGA, HDR, etc.

quizData.question: What colour does a typical Normal Map appear?
quizData.explanation: Normal maps use the RGB channels to store surface direction. This gives them a distinctive purple‑blue look.

slides.title: UV Mapping Fundamentals 🗺️
slides.content:
## Wrapping a 3D Object

**UVs** are 2D coordinates that tell Unreal how to wrap a flat texture onto a 3D mesh. Think of it as **gift wrapping paper** – the UV layout is the blueprint showing where each pattern lands.

* Every mesh has UV coordinates stored in its geometry.
* **TexCoord** node (shortcut: hold **U** + click) provides these coordinates.
* Connect TexCoord to the **UVs** input of a Texture Sample.

If a model is imported without UVs, the material won't map correctly. You'll see stretched or missing textures.

slides.title: Controlling Tiling & Offset 🧩
slides.content:
## Repeat the Pattern

Connect a **Constant2Vector** to the **Multiply** input of a TexCoord before linking to Texture Sample:

* `TexCoord * Constant2Vector(2,2)` → tiles the texture 2×2.
* Use a **Scalar Parameter** (named, expose to Material Instance) for dynamic tiling.

To **offset** (pan) the texture, add a Constant2Vector to TexCoord before multiplication. This shifts the pattern without moving the mesh.

Example: `(TexCoord + Offset) * Tiling`

quizData.question: Changing the UV tiling in the material affects the mesh's geometry.
quizData.explanation: UV tiling only changes how the texture is sampled, not the actual mesh vertices.

slides.title: Texture Import Settings ⚙️
slides.content:
## Optimise and Tweak

Double‑click any texture asset to open its settings:

* **Compression** – default is DXT for RGB, or Masks for grayscale. Normal maps should use **Normalmap** compression.
* **sRGB** – on for colour textures, off for data textures (roughness, normal).
* **Mip Maps** – lower resolution versions generated automatically. Enable for better performance.
* **Texture Group** – set to World, Character, UI, etc. for texture streaming.

For normal maps, make sure **Compression** is set to **Normalmap**, otherwise you'll get visual artifacts.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Channel Packing

To save memory, combine roughness, metallic, and AO into a single texture's R, G, B channels. Use **Component Mask** to extract each channel in the material. It's an industry standard.
